sentences.text: Date : 20-02-2023 Heard Mr. S. Munir, learned counsel for the petitioner and also heard Mr. RR Kaushik, learned Addl. PP, appearing for the State Respondent.

The petitioner, namely, Dr. Sushanta Bhattacharjya has filed an application under section 438 Cr.P.C., with prayer for pre-arrest bail as he is apprehending arrest in connection with Bongaigaon PS Case No.41/2023 under sections 376(2)(d)/493/506 IPC .

The allegation against the petitioner is that he has physical Page No.# 2/2 relationship with the informant who used to work in his clinic and impregnated her and finally the informant gave birth to a child.
The petitioner, however, did not keep his promise of maintaining the child.
It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the petitioner's wife has also lodged an FIR against the informant with allegations of blackmailing and of demanding money.

sentences.text:
I have considered the submissions at the bar and have also perused the case diary along with the statement of the victim girl recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
The victim appears to be a consenting party and she was well aware that the petitioner was a married man.
The investigation of the case also progressed considerably.

Considering all aspects and in view of my foregoing discussions, the petition is allowed and in the event of his arrest, the petitioner shall be enlarged on bail of Rs.50,000/- with a suitable surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting authority under the conditions that:
i. The petitioner will co-operate with the investigation.
ii. The petitioner will appear before the IO within 10 (ten) days; and iii. The petitioner will not exercise threats to witness and tamper with the evidence.
The instant anticipatory bail application stands disposed off.
